userStories.title: Create blog system with static TypeScript data
userStories.description: Build a blog system using Next.js App Router. Blog posts are stored as TypeScript objects in /src/data/blog/posts.ts. Each post has: slug, title, excerpt, content (HTML string), date, category, author, readTime, tags, and featured image path. Create /app/blog/page.tsx (listing with cards) and /app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx (article page with full content). Both pages must have proper metadata (title, description, OG tags). Add a BlogCard component at /src/components/BlogCard.tsx.
acceptanceCriteria: /blog page renders a grid of blog post cards with title, excerpt, date, category badge, and read time
/blog/[slug] renders individual article with full HTML content, author, date, tags, and back link
Both pages have generateMetadata with unique title, description, and OG image
TypeScript compiles without errors
No external database or CMS â€” pure static data in /src/data/blog/posts.ts
technicalNotes: site/src/data/blog/posts.ts â€” create blog post data array
site/src/app/blog/page.tsx â€” blog listing page
site/src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx â€” individual article page
site/src/components/BlogCard.tsx â€” reusable card component
Use Tailwind prose classes for article body typography

userStories.title: Write 6 SEO-optimised travel blog articles about JB for backpackers
userStories.description: Research backpacker content online and write 6 original, high-quality blog articles targeting tourists visiting Johor Bahru. Articles must be 600-900 words each, written in friendly travel-guide style, and contain keywords backpackers actually search for. Include internal links to /guide, /rooms, and /book pages. Topics: (1) Ultimate JB Food Guide for Backpackers, (2) Singapore to JB Day Trip Guide: How to Cross the Causeway, (3) Top 10 Things to Do in Johor Bahru on a Budget, (4) JB Street Food Hawker Centers You Must Visit, (5) Johor Bahru vs Singapore: Why Savvy Travellers Base Themselves in JB, (6) Hidden Gems in Johor Bahru: Beyond the Usual Tourist Spots. Each article must have a unique slug, proper SEO metadata, and be added to posts.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: All 6 articles exist in posts.ts with unique slugs, titles, excerpts, categories, dates, and tags
Each article body is 600-900 words of original, rewritten content (not copied)
Each article contains 2-3 internal links to /guide, /rooms, or /book
Articles cover: food, border crossing, budget activities, hawker centers, JB vs SG comparison, hidden gems
All articles have SEO-friendly titles with keywords like 'Johor Bahru', 'JB', 'budget', 'backpacker'

Tags should include: johor-bahru, singapore, budget-travel, food, backpacker, malaysia

userStories.title: Add RSS/Atom feed at /feed.xml for the blog
userStories.description: Create a Next.js Route Handler at /app/feed.xml/route.ts that returns a valid RSS 2.0 XML feed from the blog posts data. The feed must include: channel title, link, description, language, and item entries with title, link, description (excerpt), pubDate, category, and guid. Add a <link rel='alternate' type='application/rss+xml'> tag in layout.tsx. Also add the feed URL to robots.ts.

userStories.title: Update sitemap.ts to include all blog posts
userStories.description: Update /app/sitemap.ts to dynamically include all blog post URLs. Import the posts array from /src/data/blog/posts.ts. For each post, add an entry with url: `${baseUrl}/blog/${post.slug}`, lastModified using post.date, changeFrequency: 'monthly', and priority: 0.7. Also add the /blog listing page with priority 0.8. This ensures Google can discover and index all articles.
acceptanceCriteria: /sitemap.xml includes /blog URL with priority 0.8
